notes: Decimal amounts: 67404.044 CNH against 10000.6 USD. The point of the row is that both survive the round trip unrounded, including the third decimal place on the CNH leg.

No runUpTo and no expect, so every step must genuinely pass. Steps 05 and 05b compare the ledger's leg amounts against these two numbers as Decimals, so 10000.6 and a returned "10000.60" match, while a ledger that rounded 67404.044 to 67404.04 fails there rather than passing quietly.
Settlement is a future date. {{T+3}} resolves to three calendar days after the run date, so the trade never targets a date that has gone stale; tradeDate is the run date.
tradeReference, tradeReferenceSupplement and counterpartyReferenceNumber are free-text boxes, so they are generated per run as tradeId, the party partyTradeId and the counterparty partyTradeId.
ccpAlias is N/A and clearingBroker and counterpartyClearingBroker are blank in the sheet; none has a wrapper field, so they are left out of the payload entirely.
Party CCP and Cpty CCP (PVP / PVP) are legal-entity reference data in Baton, not trade fields, so they are recorded here and the payload carries the ordinary PVP settlement flag.
settlementCcy has no field in the wrapper, so it is recorded here only.
direction and Against list both options in the sheet. The first of each, Buy and Base, is used, matching the rest of the pack.
rate is carried as the sheet states it (2) even though 67404.044/10000.6 implies 6.74.
